posts.text: More than 60% of Russians surveyed believe that Russia bears no responsibility for the destruction in Ukraine. Only 6% think the country should be held accountable for the casualties, according to the Levada Center. The findings were presented at the conference “The Country and the World: Russian Realities 2026” by Alexey Levinson, head of the Levada Center’s Department of Socio-Cultural Research. The study found that 65% of respondents believe the United States and NATO should be held responsible for the casualties and destruction in Ukraine, while 11% blame Ukraine itself. Asked whether people like them bear any responsibility for the war, 11% of respondents answered yes, while 57% said they did not consider themselves responsible. Another 25% said they felt responsible “to some extent.” Lev Gudkov, head of the Levada Center, described the findings as a “moral catastrophe” for Russian society. Nevertheless, the sociologist noted that the 25% who consider themselves at least partly responsible for the consequences of invading another country represent a “rare occurrence” and show that “some conscience still exists.”

Nuno Felix RT @jaanikamerilo : One of the most remarkable investment stories in the technology sector comes from #Estonia . In 2021, Jaan Tallinn, co-founder of Skype, became one of the earliest investors in Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude. According to Forbes, Tallinn invested an estimated $60 million across Anthropic's first two funding rounds in 2021 and 2022. Fast forward to November 2026. Following #Anthropic 's historic IPO, Forbes estimated the value of his approximately 1.15% stake at $18.3 billion - a 305-fold return on his original investment. His estimated total net worth reached $19.7 billion. But what makes this story particularly interesting is that Tallinn's original motivation was not primarily financial. For more than a decade, he has been one of the leading advocates for AI safety, investing in research and organisations addressing the potential risks of advanced artificial intelligence. His decision to invest in Anthropic was partly motivated by a desire to influence how such powerful technology is developed. As an Estonian, and knowing how great Jaan really is, it is difficult not to feel proud. And perhaps the most interesting part of this story is that it was never just about money. tweet
